title: Cyber Safety
summary: Write safety tips and run a quick safety check for students.

steps.title: Add the header
steps.objective: Start the Cyber Safety screen with a title bar.
steps.concept: A header sits at the top of a screen and tells people where they are.
steps.expected: A title bar appears at the top of the phone.

expect.label: A Header sits in the Header zone of Cyber Safety
expect.fail: Drag the Header tool onto the glowing Header zone.

hints: Find the glowing Header tool in the toolbox on the left.
Drag it onto the glowing Header zone of the phone.
On a touch screen: tap Header, then tap the glowing Header zone.

steps.title: Name your screen
steps.objective: Give the screen a clear title.
steps.concept: The header will say “Cyber Safety”. A clear title means nobody gets lost.

expect.label: The header says exactly: Cyber Safety

hints: Click the header on the phone to select it.
Edit Text content in the Properties panel.
Type exactly: Cyber Safety

steps.title: Add the safety panel
steps.concept: The panel shows your own tips and a quick check with real-life situations. Students pick the safest choice and see why.
steps.expected: A safety panel appears in the Body zone.

expect.label: A Safety sits in the Body zone of Cyber Safety
expect.fail: Drag the Safety tool onto the glowing Body zone.

hints: Find the glowing Safety tool in the toolbox on the left.
Drag it onto the glowing Body zone of the phone.
On a touch screen: tap Safety, then tap the glowing Body zone.

steps.title: Write your first tip
steps.objective: Add a safety tip in your own words.
steps.concept: ADD TIP puts a tip on the panel. Short, clear tips are easiest to remember.

cmds: ADD TIP "Never share your password with anyone."

expect.label: The panel has at least 1 tip you wrote

hints: ADD TIP "your tip".
Put the text inside straight quotation marks.
Copy the command from the step card exactly, then press Run Commands.

steps.title: Add two more tips
steps.concept: Good safety advice covers passwords, links and asking for help.

cmds: ADD TIP "Think before you click unknown links."
ADD TIP "Tell a trusted adult if something online worries you."

expect.label: The panel has at least 3 tips you wrote

hints: Two ADD TIP lines, one per line.
Put the text inside straight quotation marks.
Copy the command from the step card exactly, then press Run Commands.

steps.title: Final style check: every colour, border, shadow and style
steps.objective: Give your screens the same colours, shapes and shadows as the model app.
steps.concept: Colours were chosen while you built each element. Now finish the whole look: every colour, background, border, corner, shadow and text style below must match the model app you tried at the start. Items you already set show a tick.
steps.expected: Your screens look exactly like the model app.
hints: Click the element on the phone first. The style box (Choose colours, borders and corners) opens by itself.
Follow the sub-steps one by one: each says which row to use and which option to click. The red dot shows where.
Text alignment and weight are in the Properties panel (right) under “Text and layout”.

steps.title: Run the safety check
steps.concept: Each situation has three choices. Pick the safest, read why, and see your score.
steps.expected: You finish the check and see a score.

expect.name: safetyDone
expect.label: You finished the safety check
expect.fail: Start the check in the running app and answer every situation.

subs.t: Press Run Project in the top bar
Start the check and answer every situation

hints: Press Run Project.
Tap Start the check.
Pick the safest answer each time.

objectives: Write clear safety tips in your own words.
Run a quick check of real-life online situations.
Learn why the safest choice is the safest.

mcqs.q: Which is a strong password habit?
a: Use a long, unique password and never share it
mcqs.why: Strong passwords are long, different for each site, and private.

mcqs.q: What should you do with a link from someone you do not know?
a: Do not click it; ask a trusted adult
mcqs.why: Unknown links can lead to harmful sites.

mcqs.q: Why does the safety check explain each answer?
a: So learners understand why a choice is safe or not
mcqs.why: Understanding the reason helps people remember.

a: Tricking someone into giving private information by pretending to be trusted
mcqs.why: Phishing messages try to steal passwords or personal details.

mcqs.q: What should you do if something online worries you?
mcqs.why: A trusted adult can help you stay safe.

tips: Never share your password with anyone.
Think before you click unknown links.
Tell a trusted adult if something online worries you.
